create.name: Jethavanarama Buddhist Monastery
create.bio:
Jethavanarama Buddhist Monastery is a Theravada monastery in the hills near Ratnapura in Sri Lanka, opened in 2017. It houses a large resident community, with more than a hundred bhikkhus as well as anagarikas, and a sister monastery for women renunciants sits a short way from the main grounds. Thousands of lay visitors come each week for talks, alms-giving and festival days, and everything the monastery offers is given without charge, supported by donations through its charitable trust.

Its teaching sets out the Buddha's path in a practical, down-to-earth way, aimed at people living ordinary family and working lives as much as at those drawn to ordination. Talks are given in Sinhala, English, Tamil and Hindi, and are streamed to followers in a dozen or so countries. This channel, started in 2021, is the monastery's English-language outlet: it posts a full-length sermon roughly every week, often two to three hours long, on subjects such as self and identity, cause and effect, death and rebirth and the two levels of truth, alongside short clips. The monastery also runs a Dhamma school for children and, when building work allows, residential insight meditation retreats with a teacher monk for each visitor.

free_resources.title: International Sermons
free_resources.description: Regular online Dhamma talks arranged for supporters abroad, from the UK and Australia to Korea, Kenya and the Gulf, booked through the monastery's charitable trust. Most of these sessions are held in Sinhala.

free_resources.title: Dhamma Programmes
free_resources.description: An overview of the monastery's talks in English, Sinhala, Tamil and Hindi, shared without charge across YouTube, podcasts and other outlets.
